triples.quote: that new doctor Katya sent for from Moscow for your unhappy brother, who will to-morrow—

triples.subject: Alexey Fyodorovitch
triples.quote: Ever since Lise took back her promise—her childish promise, Alexey Fyodorovitch—to marry you

triples.subject: Rakitin
triples.quote: that frivolous young man, would you believe it, seems to have taken it into his head to fall in love with me.

triples.subject: Rakitin
triples.quote: He had met Pyotr Ilyitch here before, and would you believe it, he is always gibing at him, growling at him, for some reason.

triples.subject: Father Zossima
triples.quote: Another contradicted this, and stated that he and his elder, Father Zossima, had broken into the monastery chest

triples.subject: Alexey Fyodorovitch
triples.quote: what wild rumors about his brother, about the Karamazovs, and about himself he had read in the course of those two months

triples.subject: Madame Hohlakov
triples.quote: And she handed Alyosha a sheet of newspaper which had been under her pillow.

triples.subject: Yulia
triples.quote: Goodness! Why are we sitting here and no coffee? Yulia, Glafira, coffee!

triples.subject: The Karamazov Case at Skotoprigonyevsk
triples.quote: The present paragraph in the paper _Gossip_ was under the heading, “The Karamazov Case at Skotoprigonyevsk.”

triples.subject: Ivan Fyodorovitch
triples.quote: I can’t trust my daughter so easily to your brother Ivan Fyodorovitch, though I still consider him the most chivalrous young man.

triples.subject: Fyodor Pavlovitch
triples.quote: knowing what a lot he has to do as it is, _vous comprenez, cette affaire et la mort terrible de votre papa_.

triples.subject: Fyodor Pavlovitch
triples.quote: Oh! not better that a son should have killed his father, I don’t defend that.

triples.subject: Yulia
triples.quote: Lise waked up and flew into a passion with Yulia and, would you believe it, slapped her in the face. That’s monstrous; I am always polite to my servants.

triples.subject: Rakitin
triples.quote: ‘You have no modern enlightened feelings, you are uninfluenced by progress, you are a mere official,’ he said, ‘and you take bribes.’

triples.subject: Madame Hohlakov
triples.quote: I got up suddenly and said to Rakitin, ‘It’s painful for me to say it, but I don’t wish to see you in my house again.’ So I turned him out.

triples.subject: Dmitri Fyodorovitch
triples.quote: When he recovered from the blow Dmitri Fyodorovitch gave him on the head, he was suffering from aberration

triples.subject: Lise
triples.quote: Lise waked up and flew into a passion with Yulia and, would you believe it, slapped her in the face.

triples.subject: Lise
triples.quote: She suddenly screamed out, ‘I hate Ivan Fyodorovitch. I insist on your never letting him come to the house again.’

triples.subject: Madame Hohlakov
triples.quote: I simply beg you to go to Lise and find out everything from her, as you alone can, and come back and tell me—me, her mother

triples.subject: Yulia
triples.quote: That’s monstrous; I am always polite to my servants. And an hour later she was hugging Yulia’s feet and kissing them.
